claim.summary: For every matrix M over F2 or F4 and every integer or Eisenstein-integer lift A in a fixed basis, rank(M)<=nu(M)<=||A||_*, where nu is the maximum support matching. A partial permutation with phases matching selected lift entries has operator norm1 and pairs with A to at least nu. The comparison survives any consistently specified basis change, positive odd-denominator clearing and explicitly divided integral deflation lifts. Thus support matching gives a rank upper bound at least as strong as this arithmetic norm criterion.

claim.summary: For every rectangular integer matrix A, rank_F2(A mod2)<=||A||_*. The same holds for Eisenstein-integer matrices embedded in C and reduced mod2 to F4, since a nonzero minor has complex modulus>=1. Nuclear norm also >=sqrt(number of nonzero residue entries). A positive odd common denominator q costs q||A||_*. For an explicitly chosen integral representative Rtilde divisible by2^v of an aggregate residue matrix, rank(def_v R)<=2^-v||Rtilde||_*. If an exact real/complex factorization of that lift A=UV is given, ||A||_*<=||U||_F||V||_F.
claim.assessment: Working elementary arithmetic-minor and singular-value inequality, checked by the same staged medium reviewer. Requires one explicit lattice lift and same domain/basis; real mass, normalized variance or a norm of a residue class alone is not such a lift. No source-sensitive contraction is supplied.
